searchText: Oh I see. So in gloas ‘the parent execution payload has been seen’ maps to bid.parent_block_hash's payload being in store.payloads ? But then, if ‘parent execution payload has been seen’ means ‘in store.payloads’ (= verified), then wouldn’t the next clause (If verification is complete: [REJECT] parent passes validation) be dead code, since anything in store.payloads already passed verify_execution_payload_envelope? 🤔 That clause only does work if a child can be accepted with the parent payload seen but not yet verified. So either seen != verified in gloas (and the on_block drop is reachable), or that REJECT clause should be removed. (Or I am not understanding something very obvious) > So in gloas ‘the parent execution payload has been seen’ maps to bid.parent_block_hash's payload being in store.payloads ? yep it reads like the following: - if parent hash has not been seen -> queue it and drop it, dont penalize the peer - if the parent has has been seen but was invalid -> drop it and penalize the peer - else import it and forward it to your peer sorry maybe im not underestanding the question, let me know if that clarifies it The second bullet point, how is it possible? If seen = valid this would read ‘If the parent is valid but was invalid’ 🤔 Im not sure if we are having troubles on terminology here… ah sorry im confusing you. Let me change `seen` from `verified` to `try to verify` so it's not like `i have seen it` it's like `i have verified it`, and i know the result of it. And the result may be applied to the subsequent checks Got it now it's very clear: “seen” = “verified, verdict known” not ‘received the bytes’. Thanks for your patience! Would changing the wording from “seen/retrieved” to “verified” make it unambiguous, or do you think everyone already reads it that way and won't trip on it like I did?

excerpts.author: luca_zanolini
excerpts.content:
Oh I see. So in gloas ‘the parent execution payload has been seen’ maps to bid.parent_block_hash's payload being in store.payloads ? 

But then,  if ‘parent execution payload has been seen’ means ‘in store.payloads’ (= verified), then wouldn’t the next clause (If verification is complete: [REJECT] parent passes validation) be dead code, since anything in store.payloads already passed verify_execution_payload_envelope? 🤔 

That clause only does work if a child can be accepted with the parent payload seen but not yet verified. So either seen != verified in gloas (and the on_block drop is reachable), or that REJECT clause should be removed. (Or I am not understanding something very obvious)

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
> So in gloas ‘the parent execution payload has been seen’ maps to bid.parent_block_hash's payload being in store.payloads ? 
yep

it reads like the following:
- if parent hash has not been seen -> queue it and drop it, dont penalize the peer
- if the parent has has been seen but was invalid -> drop it and penalize the peer
- else import it and forward it to your peer
